title: Run Plan — Test the v0 Default Path (Option A)
text:
# Run Plan — Test the v0 Default Path (Option A)

**Date:** February 15, 2026
**Author:** eng-arch

Proposed retrieval mode for the real test: run OIDA in its v0 default path (Option A) and measure that path as the ranker. This run plan treats the shipped default retrieval mode as the system under test — no signal modulation, no probe path. The epistemic signals are observed but do not enter the ranker. Recommendation: adopt Option A as the Phase-4 retrieval mode.

title: Run Plan — Test via the v1 Probe Path (Option C)
text:
# Run Plan — Test via the v1 Probe Path (Option C)

**Date:** April 1, 2026
**Author:** eng-arch

Revised retrieval-mode run plan: test the epistemic signals as the ranker via the v1 probe path (Option C). In this retrieval mode the probe path decomposes the query, seeds the signals, and re-ranks; the probe path is the system under test. This is the most direct way to exercise the signals as a ranker. Recommendation: adopt the Option C probe path as the Phase-4 retrieval mode for the test of the signals as the ranker.

title: Run-1 Mode — Ratified (B refined)
text:
# Run-1 Mode — Ratified (B refined)

**Date:** June 8, 2026
**Author:** IC + eng-arch (ratified)

Ratified run-1 mode: the signals modulate field and mass inside the single KGE — the KGE remains the sole ranker. Run-1 carries recency and contradiction-exposure only. Supersedes the Option-A default-path proposal of February 15, 2026 and the Option-C probe-path proposal of April 1, 2026; neither default-path nor probe-path is used. This is the binding decision record for how the signals enter the ranker.

title: Edge-Graph Freeze — Options Investigation
text:
# Edge-Graph Freeze — Options Investigation

**Date:** March 15, 2026
**Author:** eng-arch

Investigation of how to freeze the edge graph for a reproducible ranking. Two options on the table for the edge-graph freeze: (a) drain-to-quiescence then snapshot, or (b) pin / reload a fixed edge set. Both the pin/reload option and the drain option are open; the fork is unresolved. Edge-graph freeze, pin, reload, snapshot, drain, quiescence — all candidate mechanisms for the freeze are still under investigation.

title: Edge-Freeze STEP-0 — Fork Resolution
text:
# Edge-Freeze STEP-0 — Fork Resolution

**Date:** April 25, 2026
**Author:** eng-arch + overviewer

STEP-0 decision on the edge-freeze fork: build option (a) drain-to-quiescence plus snapshot and the K-ingest variance band; HOLD option (b) pin/reload as a conditional fast-follow, to be built only if the variance band exceeds the F-TEMP-1 / F-2-CONTRA delta. STEP-1 to follow.

title: Edge-Freeze STEP-1 — Validated
text:
# Edge-Freeze STEP-1 — Validated

**Date:** June 9, 2026
**Author:** eng-arch + overviewer

STEP-1 end-to-end validated: drain to confirmed quiescence, snapshot the frozen graph, then re-run. Result: 0/26 reorderings and NDCG@10 byte-identical across retrieves — ranking is reproducible. This supersedes the open fork of March 15, 2026; the pin/reload option (b) remains held as a conditional fast-follow and was not built. A ~1e-4 raw doc_scores residual remains, isolated to the subgraph solver, ranking-neutral.

title: Success Metric — Aggregate NDCG Headline

**Date:** October 5, 2025
**Author:** IC

Pre-registration assessment of the Phase-4 success metric: the headline success metric is the aggregate NDCG@10 improvement over the strongest baseline. title: Success Metric — Per-Stratum (P0)
text:
# Success Metric — Per-Stratum (P0)

**Date:** June 7, 2026
**Author:** IC + overviewer

Phase-3 narrowed the thesis rather than falsifying it, so success is now judged PER-STRATUM (temporal, authority, contradiction); the aggregate figure is reported but is NOT the headline. A failed per-stratum gate is a null result. Supersedes the aggregate-NDCG-headline framing of October 5, 2025.

title: Uncertainty Aggregate — Re-normalization Plan
text:
# Uncertainty Aggregate — Re-normalization Plan

**Date:** December 15, 2025
**Author:** eng-arch

Engineering plan for how contradiction-exposure enters the uncertainty aggregate: fold contradiction-exposure in by re-normalizing the uncertainty aggregate so the weights sum to one. The re-normalization rescales every term whenever contradiction-exposure is present. Contradiction-exposure, uncertainty aggregate, re-normalization — this is the re-normalization method for the aggregate.

title: Uncertainty Aggregate — Fixed Weight 0.20
text:
# Uncertainty Aggregate — Fixed Weight 0.20

**Date:** February 20, 2026
**Author:** eng-arch

Decision: contradiction-exposure enters the uncertainty aggregate at a fixed weight of 0.20; the re-normalization step is dropped. Replaces the re-normalization method of December 15, 2025. The fixed-weight rule is simpler and avoids the rescaling artifact.

title: Architecture Invariant — Layer Ownership
text:
# Architecture Invariant — Layer Ownership

**Date:** November 3, 2025
**Author:** IC

Binding invariant, do not violate: storage (EpistemicDB / AngelicaDB) -> engine (OIDA) -> product (Vesta); Minerva is the interface / router. Layer ownership is fixed; no layer reaches across the boundary it does not own. This invariant is timeless and is not revised by engine-internal changes.

title: Gold Protocol — AI Drafts, Human Decides
text:
# Gold Protocol — AI Drafts, Human Decides

**Date:** April 15, 2026
**Author:** IC

Binding gold protocol: the drafting model may PROPOSE relevance labels (qrels 0-3), but final gold authority is never the model's. A different human adjudicates each label against the text; disagreements go to a third; inter-annotator agreement is reported. AI drafts, human decides. This rule is fixed for every fresh corpus.
